{{Quote|Do not visit Gamorr.|A warning found in most galactic guidebooks|<ref name="TEA" />}}
'''Gamorr''' was an agrarian [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Gamorr system/Legends|Opoku system]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of a porcine [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]]. Its varied terrain ranged from frozen tundra to deep forests, and was considered quite pleasant by off-worlders. Nevertheless, tourism was highly discouraged to Gamorr because of the vicious lifestyle of ferocious, bloody warfare constantly being waged between rival Gamorrean clans. Prominent mushrooms were also found on Gamorr, as were native [[coolsap tree]]s.

==Description==
{{Quote|Procedures programs for visiting Gamorr consist of a single line: DO NOT VISIT GAMORR.|C-3PO|<ref name="CotJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Gamorrr.png|left|thumb|The Gamorrean landscape.]]
Gamorr occupied the third [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] from the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Opoku]] in the [[Gamorr system/Legends|Opoku system]],<ref name="TEA" /> which was itself located in the [[Galov sector/Legends|Galov sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was also within the region known as the [[The Slice/Legends|Slice]] and situated on the [[Triellus Trade Route/Legends|Triellus Trade Route]], a [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] that connected it to [[Arami]] and [[Lyran system/Legends|Lyran]].<ref name="TEA" />

Gamorr was a terrestrial world with a diameter of 15,520 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] and was orbited by two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]. Its [[Standard day/Legends|day]] lasted 28 [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] and its year consisted of 380 local days.<ref name="TEA" /> It featured a breathable [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]], a moderate hydrosphere, a temperate climate, and standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]. The free [[Water/Legends|water]] in Gamorr's atmosphere was slightly high, and as a result, severe weather and rain forests were both common on the world.<ref name="AFTGP" /> Gamorr's terrain included icy tundra in the north and equatorial inland seas,<ref name="H&R" /> as well as deciduous forests, mountains, jungles, fungus groves,<ref name="TEA" /> frozen plains,<ref name="SWS">[[The Star Wars Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''The Star Wars Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref> and swamps.<ref name="LECG" /> [[Wugguh]] was a continent on Gamorr.<ref name="MS" />

The forests and jungles of Gamorr covered a high percentage of its land mass, often overgrowing mountainous areas,<ref name="AFTGP" /> and boasted a diverse variety of flora and fauna.<ref name="RGSECR" /> Gamorrean forests were typically dense and damp, with hardwood [[Tree/Legends|trees]] that provided shelter for fungi that lived on the dark forest floors. [[Snoruuk/Legends|Snoruuks]], mobile [[Mushroom/Legends|mushrooms]] which collectively crept across the forest floor, were native to Gamorr, and [[algark stalk]]s produced a dangerous fungus found in the deep forests.<ref name="AFTGP" />

No animals larger than one [[Meter/Legends|meter]] long or high were known to inhabit the forests, but smaller animals, including [[Bird/Legends|birds]], [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]], and [[Primate/Legends|primates]], could be found in the upper levels.<ref name="AFTGP" /> [[Morrt]]s and [[Dwoob/Legends|dwoobs]] were among the animals present on Gamorr, as well as [[quizzer]]s,<ref name="MS" /> which lived in the forests of Gamorr.<ref name="CotG" /> [[Watch-beast]]s were another species that originated on Gamorr.<ref name="GaW" /> Larger animals may have existed on Gamorr at some point before being hunted to [[extinction]] by the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorreans]].<ref name="AFTGP" />

Gamorr featured a clan-based<ref name="TEA" /> and feudal system of government.<ref name="RGSECR" /> A preindustrial [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural world]],<ref name="UAA" /> it was largely self-sufficient and its inhabitants traded little with offworlders.<ref name="H&R" /> Nevertheless, it exported mercenaries<ref name="TEA" /> and [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] and imported foodstuffs, technology,<ref name="RGSECR" /> and melee weapons.<ref name="TEA" /> The mercenaries produced by Gamorr were considered to be some of the most violent in the galaxy.<ref name="KotORCG" /> The Gamorreans were unable to prevent the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] from visiting Gamorr and coercing the natives into servitude.<ref name="RGSECR" /> Scrapped hardware originating from weapons, vehicles, and gear acquired by Gamorrean mercenaries accumulated in swamps and junk heaps across Gamorr.<ref name="LECG" />

==History==
{{Quote|How did the Empire capture Gamorr without firing a cannon bolt? They landed backwards, and the Gamorreans thought they were retreating!|Jacen Solo|<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Gamorr_NEGAS.jpg|left|thumb|Another view of Gamorr.]]
The history of Gamorr was characterized by warfare and violence, with conflicts so numerous that almost no [[Historian/Legends|historians]] other than the Gamorreans themselves could genuinely understand them.<ref name="RGSECR" /> The first trade [[Starship/Legends|ship]] to land on Gamorr caused a dispute between five Gamorrean clans, who warred over the right to approach the ship. After two days of combat, the victorious Gamorreans destroyed the craft. This incident was followed by six similar events, after which the traders sent a heavily-armed vessel with orders to capture a number of Gamorreans instead of opening trade.<ref name="SWS" /> The region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] surrounding Gamorr was explored during the period between [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000]] and [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" />

Gamorr had received visitors from offworld many times by the time of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]],<ref name="KotORCG" /> and the first [[Human/Legends|Humans]] who arrived on Gamorr enslaved large numbers of the native population.<ref name="RGSECR" /> During the Great Sith War, Gamorr was considered to be under [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] occupation. The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] later drove the Sith forces away from Gamorr, and the world returned to a state of primitive isolation that continued until after the [[Jedi Civil War]]. The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] avoided Gamorr,<ref name="KotORCG" /> but it was absorbed into the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] of [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]],<ref name="TEA" /> and during the [[Dark Wars]], the planet fell under the dominion of nearly a dozen Sith [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] at various times.<ref name="KotORCG" />

During the [[New Sith Wars]], a [[Sith Academy (Gamorr)|Sith academy]] was located on Gamorr, which fell within both [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] and space controlled by the Sith.<ref name="TEA" /> While the Galactic Republic ignored Gamorr during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] due to the primitive nature of its inhabitants, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] gave special attention to the world, transporting thousands of Gamorreans offworld and employing them as mercenaries. The Gamorreans are used in dangerous frontal assaults, suffering a survival rate below 8 percent. The Hutts, displeased with the Confederacy's recruitment, negotiate a bounty deal with the Trade Federation to retain influence over their labor force. Although a number of small [[Space warfare/Legends|space battles]] occurred in nearby [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], the surface of Gamorr was never the site of combat during the conflict, and a Separatist base on its moon is later abandoned and seized by pirates.<ref name="TCWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

Gamorr was within Hutt Space during the Clone Wars, but by [[14 BBY/Legends|14 BBY]], the region's borders had shifted, leaving Gamorr outside of Hutt Space. Attempts by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to civilize Gamorr resulted in failure, with Imperial representatives staying in a small number of fortified trading ports.<ref name="TEA" />

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] was attacked by the [[Yuuzhan Vong|invaders]]. Many [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] fled to [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]], [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and Gamorr.<ref name="BP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref>

Gamorr remained largely unchanged throughout the rise and fall of galactic powers as late as the time of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Empire]] of [[Darth Krayt]], which interfered little in Gamorr's affairs due to the difficulty of convincing nobles and bureaucrats to move to the planet.<ref name="LECG" /> By [[137 ABY]], Gamorr was within the region of space known as the [[Hutt dependencies]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
[[File:Gamorrean_and_Snoruuk.jpg|left|thumb|A Gamorrean on Gamorr.]]
Gamorr's population of 500 million consisted entirely of Gamorreans,<ref name="TEA" /> a porcine [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the world,<ref name="UAA" /> and the unceasing clan wars fought by the Gamorreans brought fame to their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="AFTGP" /> While most Gamorreans who left Gamorr did so when they were sold into slavery by their clans,<ref name="SWS" /> others found employment as bodyguards, mercenaries, and professional soldiers elsewhere in the galaxy,<ref name="UAA" /> and some emigrants were simply unusually intelligent.<ref name="H&R" /> The [[Gamorrean (language)|Gamorrean]] and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] languages were spoken on Gamorr. Gamorr possessed a single colony, the nearby world of [[Pzob/Legends|Pzob]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Locations==
[[File:Gamorr_SWJ10.jpg|right|thumb|A fortress on Gamorr.]]
Gamorr was the site of at least one [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]&ndash;a landing field&ndash;<ref name="AFTGP" />and lacked a capital [[City/Legends|city]].<ref name="RGSECR" /> The most powerful and prestigious clans on the planet controlled about a dozen large fortresses, which resembled townships. Offworlders sometimes conducted trade with natives at such settlements.<ref name="AFTGP" /> [[Jugsmuk Station]], a landing field with a cluster of pre-fabs and longhouses abutting [[Jugsmuk Clanhome]], was a major port on Gamorr.<ref name="MS" />

Around [[1002 BBY]], the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] operated a [[Sith Academy (Gamorr)|Sith academy]] on the world that specialized in the training of [[Sith Warrior]]s and [[Sith Marauder|Marauders]].<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> Gamorr was also a site for [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]]; the events were made safe by the Hutts. One podracing event was located in the ruins of the ancient Gamorrean [[Carnuss Gorguul]]'s citadel.<ref name="SWG10">{{GamerCite|10|State of the Arts}}</ref> Under the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], it was the site of a [[Native Management and Industrialization Service|NAMIS]] disaster. However, the planet was never united under a single government, and remained unaligned after the fall of the Galactic Empire.

==Behind the scenes==
The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Gamorr in the Dufilvan sector (a misspelling of the true [[Dufilvian sector/Legends|Dufilvian sector]]), which is actually located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].
